units.text: EXT. QUARRY DIVING PLATFORM - DAWN
A ten-meter steel tower above a flooded granite pit.
Mist hangs on the green water.
Pigeons burst from the cliff-face at the clap of a distant gate.
A WOMAN (30s, black swimsuit, towel around her neck, a handheld voice recorder in her fist) climbs the last rung and walks to the lip of the platform.
Her bare feet leave wet prints on the grating.
She is lean and focused, with the stillness of someone who has done something ten thousand times and is afraid of the ten-thousand-and-first.
She clicks the recorder on.
Dive log, ninth of June. Wind, nothing. Water, sixty-one degrees. Platform, dry, mostly.
units.name: WOMAN

units.text: She breathes in.
Out.
Today's the one. Reverse three and a half, tuck. I've hit it in the pool. I haven't hit it here.
units.name: WOMAN

units.text: She sets the recorder on the grating.
It records her silence, then her voice.

You hit it by letting go of the thought of hitting it. That's what Coach said. That's what the last coach said. That's what the first coach said, and she was lying, because nobody ever lets go of that.
units.name: WOMAN

units.text: A gull shrieks.
She tips her head back, closes her eyes.
My name is Isolde Vantongeren. Twenty-nine. Six years since the last medal. I don't know if I'm doing this for the medal or for the girl who got it.
units.name: WOMAN

units.text: The recorder blinks.
A clock ticks inside it.
Okay. Okay.
units.name: ISOLDE

units.text: She picks up the recorder.
Rewinds.
Presses play.
...you hit it by letting go of the thought of hitting it.
units.name: WOMAN

units.text: Liar.
units.name: ISOLDE

units.text: She sets it down again.
Walks backward to the rear edge of the platform, then forward, two steps, three, springing, and lifts into the air.
The water takes her without a sound.
Rings spread across the surface and the mist shivers.
The recorder, abandoned on the grating, goes on running.
In the silence it picks up only the dripping tower, the pigeons settling, and a long, delighted shout from the water.
